transcript.text: My fridge freezer has been making a funny smell in the kitchen the last couple of days, I've cleaned it out but it's still there. Any ideas?

A persistent smell after cleaning is usually caused by something hidden—like a small spill under a shelf, rotting food in a vegetable crisper, or a blocked defrost drain letting stagnant water sit. It could also be an electrical issue if the smell is like burning plastic. To help me narrow this down safely, what is the make and model number of your fridge-freezer? This is usually on a sticker inside the unit.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]

It's a Beko, model CDA543FS, from the label inside the fridge. It's about 20 years old. The smell is a bit like hot plastic or electrical burning, more round the back than inside, now that I think about it.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. A burning plastic smell coming from the back of a fridge-freezer is a serious safety warning. It almost probably means an electrical component—such as the mains lead, plug, internal wiring, or the compressor's start relay—is overheating or shorting out. Because this involves live electricity and presents a fire risk, you must unplug the appliance immediately and not use it again until a qualified engineer has inspected it. I cannot advise on how to fix this safely as it requires specialist electrical testing.
